package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a sophisticated backdoor that enables remote, unauthorized access to systems via SSH by tampering with authentication routines. The malicious code is obfuscated, conditionally activated, and was inserted through a long-term social engineering campaign targeting the project's maintainership and release process.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: build-to-host.m4 script calls a hidden script that checks for architecture and OS, then unpacks malicious data from tests/files/bad-3-corrupt_lzma2.xz and tests/files/good-large_compressed.lzma.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During build-time, the script checks system architecture and OS, then unpacks obfuscated/encrypted payloads from test files, modifying the build process to inject a backdoor into the resulting liblzma binary.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Build scripts should not unpack or execute hidden payloads from test files, nor conditionally alter the build based on system architecture.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal build scripts only configure compilation; here, the build process is hijacked to inject malicious code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Conditional compilation for platform-specific optimizations (but not hidden payload unpacking).
key_indicators: Modification of build process to inject code

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when liblzma is loaded by sshd)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious code in liblzma.so.5.6.0 uses IFUNC to hook OpenSSH authentication routines, specifically redirecting RSA_public_decrypt to a malicious implementation.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when loaded by /usr/sbin/sshd, the code uses IFUNC to hook and redirect OpenSSH's RSA_public_decrypt function, enabling bypass of SSH authentication and remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Shared libraries should not hook authentication routines or alter cryptographic functions in unrelated processes.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: liblzma is a compression library, not an authentication or cryptography handler.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Debugging or profiling tools may hook functions, but never in production cryptographic contexts.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious payload activates only if process name is /usr/sbin/sshd and other conditions (architecture, glibc, etc.) are met.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the payload checks for specific process and environment conditions before activating, minimizing detection and targeting only high-value systems.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate libraries do not conditionally activate hidden payloads based on process name or environment.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Compression libraries should not contain logic to check for process names or system architecture for malicious activation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; such conditional activation is a hallmark of targeted malware.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated/encrypted bash stages and binary backdoor stored in test files, unpacked and injected during build.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During build-time, hidden payloads in test files are unpacked and used to modify the resulting library, embedding the backdoor.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Test files should not contain executable payloads or be used to modify production binaries.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Test data is for validation, not for delivering code to production builds.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is a clear abuse of test data.
key_indicators: Use of test data in build process

attack_chain.action: Malicious build-to-host.m4 script checks system and unpacks hidden payloads from test files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Injection of backdoor code into liblzma.so during build.

attack_chain.action: Backdoored liblzma.so is built and distributed as part of xz-utils 5.6.0/5.6.1.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of malicious library on target systems.

attack_chain.action: When loaded by /usr/sbin/sshd, the malicious library uses IFUNC to hook authentication routines.
attack_chain.leads_to: Redirection of RSA_public_decrypt, enabling SSH authentication bypass.

attack_chain.action: Conditional activation ensures payload only runs on targeted systems (amd64, glibc, systemd, etc.).
attack_chain.leads_to: Stealthy, targeted remote access for attacker.

behavioral_signatures: Build scripts unpacking or executing hidden payloads from test files
ELF shared objects using IFUNC to hook unrelated process functions
Libraries checking process names and system architecture at runtime
Redirection of cryptographic/authentication functions in sshd
file_indicators: liblzma.so.5.6.0 (increased size, changed hash, loss of hardening features)
network_indicators: No explicit C2 domain observed yet, but potential for SSH-based remote access or exfiltration via compromised authentication
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected changes in liblzma.so (hash, size, hardening features). Flag build scripts that unpack or execute code from test files. Detect IFUNC-based hooking in shared libraries, especially those loaded by sshd. Watch for libraries that check process names or system architecture at runtime. Alert on any modification or redirection of cryptographic functions in OpenSSH processes.
